why.neverMissTwice: One miss is an accident; two in a row start a new habit. Hence “never miss twice” (Clear).
why.comeback: Your last two days with habits went unchecked. Thinking “I already ruined it” is what makes people quit most; coming back with something small breaks it.
why.usualTime: Median time of your last {{sample}} check-ins of “{{name}}”. Habits at a stable time become automatic sooner.
why.weakWeekday: Your last {{sample}} days like today ({{weekday}}): {{weekdayPercent}}% vs {{averagePercent}}% overall. Lowering the bar on hard days protects consistency (2-minute rule).
why.automaticity: {{completions}} repetitions in the last 120 days. Lally et al. (2010): a median of ~66 days to automaticity, ranging from 18 to 254.
why.addMinimum: {{percent}}% of {{sample}} times in the last 30 days. The 2-minute rule (Clear): show up first, improve later.
why.addIntention: {{percent}}% of {{sample}} times in the last 30 days. Implementation intentions: deciding when and where has a medium-to-large effect (Gollwitzer & Sheeran, 2006).
why.weekUp: Share of habits done this week vs last. The 1% rule: small gains that compound.
why.projection: {{recent}} repetitions in the last 28 days; at that pace you reach ~66. An estimate, not a promise: it takes anywhere from 18 to 254 days.
why.agenda: Your toughest band over the last 30 days: {{band}} ({{percent}}%). Doing the hard thing while you have energy helps.
why.bestBand: Your last 30 days by band. Habits anchored to stable moments form faster.
why.minimumSaved: {{count}} times with the minimum version in 30 days and a streak of {{streak}}. Showing up beats intensity (2-minute rule).
why.fact: A fact from habit science (Clear, Lally, Gollwitzer).

facts.0: Every time you do a habit, you cast a vote for the person you want to become. You don't need unanimity, just a majority.
facts.1: 1.01 to the power of 365 is about 37: a little better each day, sustained, compounds. Small things matter.
facts.2: A habit takes about 66 days on average to become automatic, anywhere from 18 to 254. There is no magic 21.
facts.3: Habit stacking works: “After [something you already do], I will [new habit].” The old routine becomes your reminder.
facts.4: Make the good obvious: the book on your pillow, the shoes by the door. Your environment decides more than willpower.
facts.5: Missing one day doesn't meaningfully affect forming a habit. What hurts is giving up.
facts.6: The 2-minute rule: start with a version so small you can't say no. First, it's about showing up.
facts.7: Pair what you need to do with something you enjoy: your favorite podcast, only while you walk.
